nodes.summary: Every frontier occurrence satisfies the resource invariant at some budgets.
nodes.title: Frontier occurrences satisfy the resource invariant

nodes.summary: A property split by branches holds at the root iff it holds at some frontier occurrence.
nodes.title: Branch-split properties hold at the root iff at some leaf

nodes.summary: Increasing a depth cut beyond a terminal frontier leaves the list unchanged.
nodes.title: Deepening the cut past a terminal frontier changes nothing

nodes.summary: Every depth-cut frontier is nonempty.
nodes.title: Depth-cut frontiers are nonempty

nodes.summary: A map commuting with both steps transports the ordered frontier, preserving multiplicity.
nodes.title: Commuting maps transport the ordered frontier

nodes.summary: Step transport restricted to a preserved invariant transports the frontier and records that all its occurrences satisfy the invariant.
nodes.title: Invariant-restricted step transport of the frontier

nodes.summary: The frontier below `s`, left to right, cut at depth `k`. At depth zero it is `[s]`, even when `step s` branches. Duplicate occurrences are retained.
nodes.title: Depth-cut frontier of a binary branching step

nodes.summary: With at most `d` further depth steps and `h` further heavy steps, the frontier has at most `∑ j ∈ range (h + 1), d.choose j` occurrences. The source budget hypotheses are retained, including the strict heavy-budget inequality.
nodes.title: Binomial bound on the frontier size under depth and heavy budgets

nodes.summary: A property of every state ever on the stack holds of each collected leaf.
nodes.title: Stack invariants hold for every collected leaf

nodes.summary: With a terminal frontier and enough rounds, the final count is its total weight.
nodes.title: Final count of counting rounds is the frontier weight

nodes.summary: Counting rounds are the projection of list-output rounds to the sum of output weights.
nodes.title: Counting rounds project list-output rounds

nodes.summary: One stack round accumulating natural weights rather than a list of terminal states. The previous count is retained, and each terminal occurrence contributes its weight.
nodes.title: Weight-counting depth-first round

nodes.summary: A commuting node map transports any number of rounds. No injectivity is required.
nodes.title: Commuting maps transport any number of rounds

nodes.summary: After at least `2 * length - 1` rounds from `[s]`, the stack is empty and all terminal frontier occurrences have been collected in reverse order.
nodes.title: Enough rounds empty the stack and collect the frontier

nodes.summary: If every frontier occurrence is terminal, exactly `2 * length - 1` rounds process the tree below `s`, preserving the tail `r` and prepending its reversed frontier to `out`. The terminal-frontier hypothesis is essential: a depth cut may contain branching states.
nodes.title: Exact round count for traversing a terminal frontier

nodes.summary: A commuting node map transports one stack round and its accumulated output.
nodes.title: Commuting maps transport one depth-first round

nodes.summary: An empty work stack is fixed by any number of rounds.
nodes.title: An empty work stack is fixed by every round

nodes.summary: One depth-first round on `(stack, output)`. Terminal states are prepended to the output; a branching state is replaced by its left child followed by its right child.
nodes.title: One depth-first round of binary branching

nodes.summary: The depth budget bounds the stack by `D + 1` at every round; each pending state satisfies the resource invariant. This is a list-size bound, not a machine-space model.
nodes.title: Depth budget bounds the depth-first stack size

nodes.summary: A depth allowance covering the remaining depth budget produces only terminal states.
nodes.title: A large enough depth cut yields only terminal states

nodes.summary: A natural-valued weight additive across each branch equals the sum of the frontier weights, even when the frontier is cut before termination.
nodes.title: Additive weight of the root is the sum over the frontier

nodes.summary: With a terminal frontier, pending and collected occurrences together never exceed its length, including before traversal is complete.
nodes.title: Pending plus collected occurrences are bounded by the frontier length

nodes.summary: One round does not decrease the combined number of pending and collected occurrences.
nodes.title: A round does not decrease pending plus collected occurrences

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
